05 ADHD and sleep · class card

Orexin antagonists

orexin receptor antagonists · suvorexant · lemborexant · daridorexant

Key point
  • Suvorexant, lemborexant and daridorexant block orexin (hypocretin) receptors less wake drive sleep, for insomnia
  • In narcolepsy orexin can already be low blocking its receptors worsens the loss: contraindicated
  • Avoid in and with a strong cytochrome P450 3A4 (CYP3A4) inhibitor; physical dependence: none or low Liver diseaseIn practice: use is not recommended only in severe hepatic impairmentMild or moderate disease: no dose adjustment required
Drugs

Belsomra: orexin receptor antagonist MnemonicMnemonicSuv-orex-ant: the orexin antagonist is in the name Suvorexant dosingOnce a night at mostWithin 30 minutes of bedAt least 7 hours left before waking

Lemborexant Dayvigo: same class, same narcolepsy contraindication

Daridorexant Quviviq: same class, same narcolepsy contraindication

Mechanism

Orexin A and B from the lateral hypothalamus both orexin receptor types wakefulness

Both receptors blocked wake drive thought to be suppressed sleep comes and lasts

Narcolepsy: orexin output can already be low the blockade deepens the deficit

Uses

Insomnia, trouble falling or staying asleep, after cognitive behavioral therapy for insomnia

Adverse effects

Somnolence: most common with suvorexant; next-day impairment, including driving, grows with dose

Headache, dizziness, abnormal dreams, upper respiratory tract infection

Sleep paralysis, hypnagogic or hypnopompic hallucinations and cataplexy-like symptoms, more at higher doses

Complex sleep behaviors such as sleep-walking or sleep-driving: stop the drug

Suicidal ideation: dose-related

: none or low DependenceIn practice: suvorexant is Schedule IVAbuse studies: effects similar to zolpidem on subjective ratingsTrials: no physical dependence found

Narcolepsy made worseOrexin can already be deficient; blocking its receptors worsens the deficiency, and the drug itself can bring sleep paralysis and cataplexy-like symptoms

If narcolepsy is on the problem list and a sleep aid is requested, choose any option other than an orexin antagonist.

Practice
  1. 24-year-old man with narcolepsy on modafinil asks for a sleep aid: lies awake 2 hours most nights for a month sleep hygiene reviewed; no alcohol or opioids; no depression examination normal · urine drug screen negative → Suvorexant → suvorexant blocks orexin receptors, and narcolepsy can stem from orexin deficiency, so it is contraindicated; cognitive behavioral therapy for insomnia comes first, and zolpidem acts at the benzodiazepine site
  2. 47-year-old woman on suvorexant for chronic insomnia drowsy and slow at work for 4 days began clarithromycin-based Helicobacter pylori therapy 5 days ago same nightly dose · 8 hours in bed · no alcohol · examination normal → Clarithromycin raising the suvorexant level → clarithromycin blocks cytochrome P450 3A4, the enzyme that clears suvorexant, so exposure climbs and sleepiness carries into the day; she drinks no alcohol and spends a full night in bed
  3. 58-year-old man with decompensated cirrhosis from hepatitis C wakes at 3 AM and cannot fall back asleep, most nights for 6 months asks for a sleeping pill; no alcohol for 2 years ascites · jaundice · no asterixis → Suvorexant → an orexin antagonist is not recommended in liver disease, and decompensated cirrhosis is the severe impairment its label names; stimulus control and sleep restriction are behavioral parts of cognitive behavioral therapy for insomnia
